title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Adjusting the Standards for Jurisdiction over First-Instance Civil and Commercial Cases by High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts
keywords_en: court jurisdiction over first-instance civil and commercial cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Adjusting the Jurisdictional Standards for First Instance Civil and Commercial Cases Heard by High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts

Fa Fa [2008] No. 10

To: All high people's courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

For the purpose of implementing the amended Civil Procedure Law and further strengthening the trial supervision and guidance functions of the Supreme People's Court and the high people's courts, the following notice is hereby given regarding the adjustment of the jurisdictional standards for first instance civil and commercial cases heard by high people's courts and intermediate people's courts:

I. High People's Courts Have Jurisdiction Over the Following First Instance Civil and Commercial Cases

The High People's Courts of Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang may have jurisdiction over first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of 200 million yuan or more, and first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of 100 million yuan or more where the domicile of one of the parties is not within their respective jurisdictions or where the case is foreign-related or related to Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan.

The High People's Courts of Tianjin, Chongqing, Shandong, Fujian, Hubei, Hunan, Henan, Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Guangxi, Anhui, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Shanxi, and Hainan may have jurisdiction over first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of 100 million yuan or more, and first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of 50 million yuan or more where the domicile of one of the parties is not within their respective jurisdictions or where the case is foreign-related or related to Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan.

The High People's Courts of Gansu, Guizhou, Xinjiang, Inner Mongolia, and Yunnan, and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region may have jurisdiction over first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of 50 million yuan or more, and first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of 20 million yuan or more where the domicile of one of the parties is not within their respective jurisdictions or where the case is foreign-related or related to Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan.

The High People's Courts of Qinghai, Ningxia, and Tibet may have jurisdiction over first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of 20 million yuan or more, and first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of 10 million yuan or more where the domicile of one of the parties is not within their respective jurisdictions or where the case is foreign-related or related to Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan.

II. Intermediate People's Courts Have Jurisdiction Over the Following First Instance Civil and Commercial Cases

The jurisdictional standards for first instance civil and commercial cases heard by intermediate people's courts shall be determined by the respective high people's courts, but shall meet the following conditions:

For intermediate people's courts under the jurisdiction of Beijing and Shanghai, and intermediate people's courts located in provincial capitals, cities with independent planning status, and economically more developed cities within the jurisdictions of Guangdong, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang, they may have jurisdiction over first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 50 million yuan, and first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 20 million yuan where the domicile of one of the parties is not within their respective jurisdictions or where the case is foreign-related or related to Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan. Other intermediate people's courts may have jurisdiction over first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 20 million yuan, and first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 8 million yuan where the domicile of one of the parties is not within their respective jurisdictions or where the case is foreign-related or related to Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan.

For intermediate people's courts under the jurisdiction of Tianjin, intermediate people's courts in urban districts under the jurisdiction of Chongqing, and intermediate people's courts located in provincial capitals, cities with independent planning status, and economically more developed cities within the jurisdictions of Shandong, Fujian, Hubei, Hunan, Henan, Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Guangxi, Anhui, Jiangxi, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Shanxi, and Hainan, they may have jurisdiction over first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 8 million yuan, and first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 3 million yuan where the domicile of one of the parties is not within their respective jurisdictions or where the case is foreign-related or related to Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan. Other intermediate people's courts may have jurisdiction over first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 5 million yuan, and first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 2 million yuan where the domicile of one of the parties is not within their respective jurisdictions or where the case is foreign-related or related to Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan.

For intermediate people's courts located in provincial capitals within the jurisdictions of Gansu, Guizhou, Xinjiang, Inner Mongolia, and Yunnan, they may have jurisdiction over first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 3 million yuan, and first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 2 million yuan where the domicile of one of the parties is not within their respective jurisdictions or where the case is foreign-related or related to Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan. Other intermediate people's courts may have jurisdiction over first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 2 million yuan, and first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 1 million yuan where the domicile of one of the parties is not within their respective jurisdictions or where the case is foreign-related or related to Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan.

For intermediate people's courts within the jurisdictions of Qinghai, Ningxia, and Tibet, they may have jurisdiction over first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 1 million yuan, and first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of not less than 500,000 yuan where the domicile of one of the parties is not within their respective jurisdictions or where the case is foreign-related or related to Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan.

III. Cases involving marriage, inheritance, family, property services, personal injury compensation, traffic accidents, labor disputes, and group disputes shall generally be under the jurisdiction of basic people's courts.

IV. For cases that are major, difficult, novel, or have general significance in the application of law, the higher people's court may, in accordance with Article 39 of the Civil Procedure Law, decide on its own to hear such cases, or decide to hear them upon the request of a lower people's court.

V. For maritime and admiralty cases subject to exclusive jurisdiction, foreign-related civil and commercial cases subject to centralized jurisdiction, and intellectual property cases, the existing provisions shall apply.

VI. The jurisdictional standards for first instance civil and commercial cases within the military heard by military courts shall be implemented with reference to the standards of local people's courts at the corresponding level.

VII. If a high people's court deems it truly necessary, it may set standards appropriately higher than those provided in this notice. For intermediate people's courts in impoverished areas within its jurisdiction, the standards may be appropriately lowered.

VIII. Each high people's court shall submit its jurisdictional standards for cases at the corresponding level within its jurisdiction to this Court for approval before March 5, 2008. Without approval, such standards shall not serve as the basis for determining level-based jurisdiction.

If any issues arise during the implementation of this notice, please promptly report them to this Court.

February 3, 2008
